title: LEN, LEFT and RIGHT: count and cut

screens.prompt: In B2, count how many characters the code in A2 has, spaces included.

hints.syntax: LEN takes one argument, the cell to measure: =LEN(A2).
hints.func-len: LEN answers how long the code is, not what it says.
hints.require-ref: Measure A2, not a typed copy of the code.
hints.value: Count every character of Invoice 2026-03, the space between word and year included.
hints.error: The grader wants the character count, so a total that skips the space reads 14 and fails.

reject.why: the closing bracket is missing, so nothing runs
that returns the whole code as text, not a count of its characters
LEN with nothing to measure has no length to report
dropping one character undercounts a fifteen-character code
the code typed into the formula, so a corrected code would not change the count
a length divided by zero returns #DIV/0!

screens.prompt: In B2, cut the first three characters of A2 to get the document prefix.

hints.syntax: =LEFT(A2,3): the text first, then the number of characters to keep.
hints.func-left: The prefix sits at the start, so LEFT is the cutter you want here.
hints.require-ref: Cut from A2, not from typed text.
hints.value: The first three characters of Invoice 2026-03 are I, n and v.
hints.error: A count of 4 returns Invo; the grader expects Inv.

reject.why: the closing bracket is missing, so nothing runs
RIGHT cuts from the end and returns 0-3, which is the suffix rather than the prefix
without a count LEFT defaults to one character, and the prefix is three
two characters gives In, and the prefix needs three
the code typed into the formula, so a new code would keep the old prefix
a negative count is impossible and LEFT returns #VALUE!

screens.prompt: In B2, cut the last four characters of A2 to get the year and month.

hints.syntax: =RIGHT(A2,4): the text first, then how many characters to keep from the end.
hints.func-right: The year and month sit at the end, so this calls for the end-cutter.
hints.value: The last four characters are 6, -, 0 and 3.
hints.error: A count of 5 returns 026-03, which is the month plus one digit too many.

reject.why: the closing bracket is missing, so nothing runs
LEFT cuts from the start and returns Invo, which is not the year
the default is one character, and the year and month need four
three characters gives -03, and the year's last digit is missing
the code typed into the formula, so a new code would keep the old year
a negative count is impossible and RIGHT returns #VALUE!

docs.explain:
LEN counts characters, spaces included. Invoice 2026-03 runs to 15: the seven letters, the space, four year digits, the hyphen and two month digits. Counting the space is what makes 15 right and 14 wrong.

LEFT(A2,3) keeps the first three characters and returns Inv, the document prefix. RIGHT(A2,4) keeps the last four and returns 6-03, the final digit of the year, the hyphen and the month. Both take a count you supply, so neither knows anything about the code.

A typed count is fine while every code has the same shape. The first code with a longer prefix gets cut in the wrong place, and LEFT returns the wrong letters instead of an error. That is the point at which FIND takes over the counting.

errors.text: A negative count gives LEFT or RIGHT nothing to cut, so the cell shows #VALUE!.
A count that suits one code takes the wrong characters from a code of a different length.
The function is spelled LN or LEF, and Excel returns #NAME?.

docs.atWork: Splitting a supplier reference into its document type and the period it covers.
docs.outcome: Measure a string, then cut fixed pieces from either end.

seo.title: LEN, LEFT and RIGHT in Excel
seo.description: Invoice 2026-03 is 15 characters, space included. LEFT gives Inv, RIGHT gives 6-03, and a typed count stops working the moment the prefix changes length.
